definition_en: to make something by putting parts together
core_image: 一堆积木被一双小手搭成一座小塔
scene: 桌上的一堆积木被一双小手搭成小塔。They build a tower with blocks.
sceneCN: 这里 build 是「搭建」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他们用积木搭起一座塔。

senses.title: To put materials together into a structure
senses.definition: to put materials together to make a building or structure
senses.definitionCN: 把材料组合起来，做成建筑或结构
senses.example: They build a tower with blocks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用积木搭起一座塔。
senses.why: Build goes back to Old English byldan, 'to construct', and its picture is materials laid one on another until a structure stands.
senses.whyCN: build 来自古英语 byldan「建造」，画面是把材料一层层垒起来，直到立成一座结构。

senses.title: To develop something gradually
senses.definition: to create or develop something gradually, such as a team or trust
senses.definitionCN: 把队伍、信任等一点一点培养起来
senses.example: The coach built a strong team.
senses.why: A team or a trust grows piece by piece like a wall, so the building verb also covers slowly making something abstract.
senses.whyCN: 队伍和信任也像墙一样一块块长起来，所以这个建造的动词也指慢慢做成抽象的东西。

senses.title: The shape and size of a person's body
senses.definition: the shape and size of a person's body
senses.definitionCN: 一个人身体的骨架与胖瘦高矮
senses.example: He has a strong build.
senses.why: The noun build names how a body is put together, as if it too had been constructed.
senses.whyCN: 名词 build 指身体被「构造」成的样子。

senses.title: A rabbit, in children's speech
senses.definition: a rabbit, used especially by and to children

senses.example: The bunny hops across the lawn.
senses.why: Bunny is a child's word made from the old dialect bun, 'rabbit', plus the friendly ending -y, so it sounds smaller and softer than rabbit.

senses.example: Children wait for the Easter bunny.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们等着复活节兔子。
senses.why: Easter folklore gave the rabbit a job of bringing eggs, and that figure is called the Easter bunny.
senses.whyCN: 复活节传说让兔子承担送蛋的角色，这个形象就被叫作 Easter bunny。

definition_en: used to show who does something or how it is done
core_image: 一个人站在门边，把钥匙递给身旁的朋友
scene: 一个人站在门边，把钥匙递给身旁的朋友。She goes to school by bike.
sceneCN: 这里 by 是「乘坐」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她骑自行车上学。

senses.title: By means of a vehicle or method
senses.definition: by means of a vehicle, tool or method
senses.definitionCN: 借助某种交通工具、工具或办法
senses.example: She goes to school by bike.
senses.why: By originally meant 'near, alongside'; a vehicle carries you alongside the journey, so by bike names the means of travel.
senses.whyCN: by 原意是「靠近、在旁边」；交通工具一路带着你走，于是 by bike 标出出行的手段。

senses.title: Beside or next to
senses.definition: beside or next to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 在某人某物的旁边
senses.example: He sat by the window.
senses.why: Being beside something is the oldest sense of by, and it survives unchanged in phrases of place.
senses.whyCN: 在事物旁边是 by 最古老的意思，在表示地点的短语里原样保留下来。

senses.title: Through the action of a person
senses.definition: showing who made or did something
senses.definitionCN: 标出某事物是谁做成的
senses.example: The cake was made by her mother.
senses.why: The maker stands by the finished thing as its author, so by marks the person behind an action or product.
senses.whyCN: 制作者站在成品旁边，是它的主人，所以 by 标出动作或成品背后的人。

senses.title: Not later than a stated time
senses.definition: not later than a stated time or date
senses.definitionCN: 不晚于某个时间或日期
senses.example: Finish it by Friday.
senses.why: The deadline is a point you come alongside, so by Friday means reaching that point no later than Friday.
senses.whyCN: 期限是一个你要挨上去的时间点，所以 by Friday 表示最晚到周五为止。

senses.title: Past a place, as an adverb
senses.definition: past a place or person
senses.definitionCN: 从某处或某人旁边经过
senses.example: The bus went by without stopping.
senses.why: Moving past something means passing alongside it, which is why the adverb by means 'past'.
senses.whyCN: 从某物旁过去就是与它擦身而过，所以副词 by 表示「经过」。

definition_en: a place where people stay in tents or simple shelters
core_image: 湖边搭着几顶帐篷，中间升起一小堆火
scene: 湖边搭着几顶帐篷，中间升起一小堆火。We camp by the lake for two nights.
sceneCN: 这里 camp 是「营地」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们在这湖边露营两晚。

senses.title: A place where people stay in tents
senses.definition: a place where people live temporarily in tents or huts
senses.definitionCN: 人们临时搭帐篷或住小屋的地方
senses.example: The camp by the lake was quiet at night.
senses.exampleCN: 湖边的营地夜里很安静。
senses.why: Camp came from Latin campus, 'field', through French, and first named the field where an army set up its tents.
senses.whyCN: camp 经法语来自拉丁语 campus「田野」，最初指军队搭帐篷驻扎的那片野地。

senses.title: To stay in a tent or temporary shelter
senses.definition: to stay outdoors in a tent or temporary shelter
senses.definitionCN: 在户外搭帐篷或住临时住所
senses.example: We camp by the lake for two nights.
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so camp names the act of setting up and staying at such a place.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，camp 表示搭起营地并在那里住下的行为。

senses.title: A side in a dispute or debate
senses.definition: one side in a disagreement, whose members share a view
senses.definitionCN: 争执或争论中观点相同的一方
senses.example: The two camps in the debate never agree.
senses.exampleCN: 争论中的两派从不让步。
senses.why: People who share a view are grouped as if they lived in the same camp, so the word also means a side in a dispute.
senses.whyCN: 观点相同的人被看作住在同一个营地里，于是这个词也指争执中的一方。

items.cn: 拉丁语 campus 意为「田野、平地」。

items.cn: 法语借入作 camp，指军队驻扎的野外。

items.en: The word first named a soldier's field base.
items.cn: 这个词最初指士兵的野外基地。

items.en: Later it named any stay in tents.
items.cn: 后来它指任何住帐篷的户外停留。

items.en: Camp names tents, holidays and groups.
items.cn: 现代英语中它指帐篷、假期活动与阵营。

senses.example: She cuts a carrot into small pieces.
senses.why: Carrot came into English from French carotte, from Latin carota, the name of this orange root.

senses.example: The bonus is a carrot to work harder.
senses.exampleCN: 奖金是让人更卖力干活的诱饵。

senses.whyCN: 挂在驴子前面的胡萝卜引它往前走，于是这种蔬菜的名字成了「诱人奖励」的画面。

definition_en: a drawing or film made in a simple, amusing style
core_image: 屏幕上几个线条简单的小人正在追着一个圆球跑
scene: 屏幕上几个线条简单的小人正在追着一个圆球跑。The children laugh at the cartoon.

senses.title: A humorous or satirical drawing
senses.definition: a drawing, often humorous or satirical, as in a newspaper
senses.definitionCN: 常带滑稽或讽刺意味的画，如报纸上的漫画
senses.example: He drew a cartoon of the teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他画了一幅老师的漫画。
senses.why: Cartoon came from Italian cartone, 'thick paper', because painters first sketched a design on heavy paper; the word then named the drawing itself.
senses.whyCN: cartoon 来自意大利语 cartone「厚纸」，因为画家先在厚纸上画草图，这个词后来就指画本身。

senses.title: An animated film
senses.definition: a film made from a series of drawn images that appear to move
senses.definitionCN: 由一连串画面连成、看起来会动的影片
senses.example: The children laugh at the cartoon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们看着动画片大笑。
senses.why: When the drawings are put in sequence and moved, the result is an animated film, so cartoon also names the cartoon film.

senses.title: A large hole in rock or the ground
senses.definition: a large natural hole in rock or under the ground
senses.definitionCN: 岩体里或地下天然形成的大洞
senses.example: They find a cave behind the waterfall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在瀑布后面发现一个山洞。
senses.why: Cave came through French from Latin cavus, 'hollow', so the word names a hollow space inside rock.
senses.whyCN: cave 经法语来自拉丁语 cavus「空的」，命名的是岩石里空出来的那块地方。

senses.title: To fall in or collapse
senses.definition: to fall inward or collapse, in the phrase cave in
senses.definitionCN: 向里塌下去，如 cave in
senses.example: The roof caved in under the snow.
senses.why: A hollow can collapse into itself, and English describes that falling in with cave in.
senses.whyCN: 空腔会向自身内部塌下去，英语用 cave in 描述这种塌陷。

senses.title: To give way under pressure
senses.definition: to yield to pressure or demands, in the phrase cave in
senses.definitionCN: 顶不住压力而让步
senses.example: The government caved in to the protests.
senses.exampleCN: 政府在抗议面前让步了。
senses.why: A person who gives way is like a roof caving in: the resistance collapses, so cave in also means to yield.
senses.whyCN: 顶不住的人就像塌下去的屋顶，抵抗力垮了，所以 cave in 也表示屈服。

senses.title: Low in price
senses.definition: costing little money
senses.definitionCN: 花的钱很少
senses.example: The shoes are cheap in this shop.
senses.why: Cheap goes back to Old English cēap, 'bargain, trade'; a good cheap was a good bargain, and the word narrowed to low price.
senses.whyCN: cheap 来自古英语 cēap「交易、买卖」，good cheap 原指买得划算，后来词义收窄为价钱低。

senses.title: Of low quality
senses.definition: made poorly, so that it does not last or work well
senses.definitionCN: 做得粗糙、不耐用或不好用
senses.example: The chair felt cheap and broke in a week.
senses.exampleCN: 那把椅子一看就廉价，一周就坏了。
senses.why: Things that cost little are often made with poor materials, so cheap also judges the quality of the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 价钱低的东西常用差材料做成，所以 cheap 也评判东西本身的质量。

senses.title: Mean or unfair
senses.definition: unfair or ungenerous in a way that lowers opinion of someone
senses.definitionCN: 手段低劣或出手小气，让人看不起
senses.example: That was a cheap trick.
senses.why: A person who spends little may also give little in other ways, so cheap came to describe mean behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 只肯花小钱的人，在别的方面也常给得少，于是 cheap 用来形容小气、低劣的行为。

definition_en: a farm bird kept for eggs and meat, or its meat
core_image: 一只白母鸡在院子里低头啄食，旁边是一篮鸡蛋
scene: 院子里一只白母鸡低头啄食，旁边是一篮鸡蛋。The chicken runs across the yard.
sceneCN: 这里 chicken 是「鸡」（第 01 个义项）；句意是鸡跑过院子。

senses.title: The farm bird
senses.definition: a farm bird kept for its eggs or meat
senses.definitionCN: 为取蛋或取肉而饲养的家禽
senses.example: The chicken runs across the yard.
senses.why: Chicken goes back to Old English cicen, first a young fowl, and later the whole farm bird.
senses.whyCN: chicken 来自古英语 cicen，最初指小鸡，后来泛指这种家禽。

senses.title: The meat of that bird
senses.definition: the meat of a chicken used as food
senses.definitionCN: 这种家禽供食用的肉
senses.example: We had chicken for dinner.
senses.why: When the bird is cooked and served, the same name covers the meat on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 家禽被做好端上桌时，同一个名字就指盘里的肉。

senses.title: A coward, in informal use
senses.definition: a person who is easily frightened, in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语里指胆小怕事的人
senses.example: Don't be a chicken.
senses.why: A chicken runs from anything that frightens it, so the bird's name became an informal word for a coward.
senses.whyCN: 鸡一受惊就跑，于是这种鸟的名字成了口语里「胆小鬼」的说法。

definition_en: a young person who is not yet an adult
core_image: 一个小女孩蹲在沙滩上，用湿沙堆起一座小城堡
scene: 沙滩上一个小女孩蹲着，用湿沙堆起一座小城堡。The child builds a castle in the sand.
sceneCN: 这里 child 是「孩子」（第 01 个义项）；句意是这个孩子在沙里堆城堡。

senses.title: A young person
senses.definition: a young person who is not yet an adult
senses.definitionCN: 还没有成年的年幼的人
senses.example: The child builds a castle in the sand.
senses.exampleCN: 这个孩子在沙里堆城堡。
senses.why: Child goes back to Old English cild, 'infant, young person', and youth is its whole centre.
senses.whyCN: child 来自古英语 cild「幼儿、年幼者」，年幼正是它的全部核心。

senses.title: A son or daughter of any age
senses.definition: someone's son or daughter, even when grown up
senses.definitionCN: 某人的儿子或女儿，即使已经成年
senses.example: Their children are grown up now.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的孩子现在都长大了。
senses.why: To a parent the relationship lasts past childhood, so child also means one's son or daughter at any age.
senses.whyCN: 对父母来说这层关系会越过童年一直延续，所以 child 也指任何年龄的儿女。

senses.title: Something produced by an era or cause
senses.definition: something produced by a particular time or cause
senses.definitionCN: 某个时代或原因孕育出来的东西
senses.example: This song is a child of its time.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌是它那个时代的产物。
senses.why: What an era brings forth is raised by it the way a parent raises a child, so the word can name a product of its time.
senses.whyCN: 一个时代孕育出的东西，就像父母养大的孩子，所以这个词可以指某个时代的产物。
